clips.title: Docker Multi-Stage Builds - Fast and Efficient Dockerfiles
clips.why: A multi-stage build from start to finish, and what it does to the size of the image.
look: The build stage with the full toolchain, and the final stage that copies in only the result.
The comparison of image sizes at the end.
clips.after: Our final stage gets only package.json, the production node_modules and dist/, so no compiler or source ever runs next to the gateway's key.

clips.title: Docker Image BEST Practices - From 1.2GB to 10MB
clips.why: Why the order of the steps in a Dockerfile decides how fast it builds.
look: How Docker reuses a layer when its inputs did not change.
How the order of the steps decides which layers can be reused.
clips.after: Our Dockerfile copies package.json and the lockfile and runs npm ci before it copies src/, for exactly this reason.

clips.title: STOP using Docker Image TAGS | Digests and Digital Signatures explained
clips.why: Why a tag such as node:24-bookworm-slim is not a promise, and how a digest fixes that.
look: Tags can be moved to a different image, by the publisher or by an attacker with access to the registry.
A digest is computed from the image content, so it cannot be moved.
clips.after: Both FROM lines in our Dockerfiles carry @sha256: digests, and only a reviewed pull request changes them.

clips.title: 🛡️ Docker Security: Running Containers as Non-Root User - Best Practices
clips.why: Short and practical: why root in a container is a risk, and two ways to avoid it.
look: The risks of a container process that runs as root (UID 0).
The USER instruction in the Dockerfile, and the --user flag on docker run.
clips.after: Our images end with USER 10001:10001, and the pods add runAsNonRoot so a root image would not even start.

practice.q: Why does the final stage of our Dockerfile start again FROM the base image instead of continuing the build stage?

options.text: So the final image has only what runs, without TypeScript, source or test tools
options.why: Every tool left in the image is a tool an attacker could use. The second stage copies in only package.json, production node_modules and dist/.

options.text: Because Docker allows only one RUN per stage
options.why: A stage can have as many RUN steps as it likes.
Layer caching makes builds fast. The second stage is about what ends up in the image.

practice.q: Start the container so that nothing inside it can write any file.
practice.hint: One flag, two words joined by a hyphen.
practice.why: --read-only makes the whole container filesystem read-only. If a service needs scratch space, add --tmpfs /tmp.

practice.q: Make the running process a user without root rights.
practice.hint: The user and group id the platform's images and pods use.
practice.why: A non-root user cannot change the root-owned files in /app, and the pods require runAsNonRoot.

practice.q: docker stop takes 10 seconds and the exit code is 137. What is missing?

options.why: The filesystem has nothing to do with how the process reacts to a stop signal.
EXPOSE only documents the port. It does not change how the process stops.

options.text: A SIGTERM handler that closes the server and exits
options.why: Without it Node ignores SIGTERM, Docker waits its grace time and sends SIGKILL: 128 + 9 = 137.

practice.q: Put the Dockerfile's build stage in the order that keeps the slow install cached.
items: FROM the pinned base AS build
RUN npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev
practice.why: The package files change rarely, so the install layer is reused while the source changes every day.
